name: llm_wiki
description: LLM Wiki is a cross-platform desktop application that turns your documents into an organized, interlinked knowledge base — automatically. Instead of traditional RAG (retrieve-and-answer from scratch every time), the LLM incrementally builds and maintains a persistent wiki from your sources。
one_liner: A desktop app that reads through all your documents and automatically builds a tidy, cross-linked wiki out of them, instead of you manually organizing notes.
buyer: A researcher, consultant, or small team drowning in PDFs and reports who wants a self-organizing knowledge base without manual tagging.
business_use_cases: A research lab feeds years of papers and reports into it to get an instantly browsable internal wiki instead of a folder of unsearchable PDFs.
A consulting firm builds a client-knowledge wiki automatically from meeting notes and reports, cutting the time analysts spend organizing findings.
A journalist or investigator organizes source documents on a long-running investigation into a searchable, linked knowledge base.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted/managed version for teams that don't want to run it themselves, priced per seat.
Sell a one-time 'wiki migration' service that ingests a client's existing document archive and delivers a finished knowledge base.

steal_this: Run it against a local nonprofit or small firm's shared drive of old reports this weekend and hand them back a working internal wiki as a paid pilot.
